author: James Clear
quote: You do not rise to the level of your goals. You fall to the level of your systems.
refresher: A goal names the destination; a system determines what happens on an ordinary Tuesday. Improve the recurring action that produces the result.

James Clear · Goals and systems

author: James Clear
quote: Your identity emerges out of your habits. Every belief is learned and conditioned through experience.
refresher: Small actions give you evidence for the person you want to become. Let one repeatable behavior reinforce that identity today.

links.title: Lally and colleagues · How habits form (research abstract)
James Clear · Goals and systems

author: James Clear
quote: Habit stacking: identify a current habit you already do each day and then stack your new behavior on top.
refresher: Attach a new behavior to a reliable cue you already have: after making coffee, read one page. The existing routine supplies the reminder.

links.title: BJ Fogg · How motivation, ability, and prompts shape habits
James Clear · Goals and systems

author: James Clear
quote: When you start a new habit, it should take less than two minutes to do. Scale it down (e.g. “Run three miles” becomes “Tie my running shoes”)
refresher: Shrink the entrance to a habit until starting feels easy. You are practicing showing up before you increase the difficulty.

links.title: BJ Fogg · How motivation, ability, and prompts shape habits
James Clear · Goals and systems

author: James Clear
quote: A simple rule: never miss twice. Missing once is an accident. Missing twice is the start of a new habit.
refresher: One missed day need not become a new pattern. Make the next repetition small enough to restart without a dramatic comeback.

links.title: Lally and colleagues · How habits form (research abstract)
James Clear · Goals and systems

author: James Clear
quote: Create an environment where doing the right thing is as easy as possible.
refresher: Arrange your surroundings so the useful action takes fewer steps. Put the book where your hand would otherwise find your phone.

links.title: BJ Fogg · How motivation, ability, and prompts shape habits
James Clear · Goals and systems

author: Cal Newport
quote: When you switch from some Task A to another Task B, your attention doesn't immediately follow - a residue of your attention remains stuck thinking about the original task.
refresher: Switching tasks has a hidden cost: some attention remains with the previous one. Batch interruptions and give demanding work an uninterrupted stretch.

links.title: University of Washington · A plan for returning to interrupted work
Cal Newport · On deep breaks

author: Cal Newport
quote: Busyness as a Proxy for Productivity: In the absence of clear indicators of what it means to be productive and valuable in their jobs, many knowledge workers turn back toward an industrial indicator of productivity: doing lots of stuff in a visible manner.
refresher: Visible activity can substitute for useful output. Before filling the day, name the concrete result that would make it worthwhile.

links.title: Paul Graham · Maker’s schedule, manager’s schedule
Cal Newport · On deep breaks

author: Cal Newport
quote: Deep Work: Professional activities performed in a state of distraction-free concentration that push your cognitive capabilities to their limit. These efforts create new value, improve your skill, and are hard to replicate.
refresher: Deep work stretches a valuable skill without distraction. Reserve a specific block for one demanding task, with a clear stopping point.

links.title: Paul Graham · Maker’s schedule, manager’s schedule
Cal Newport · On deep breaks

author: Cal Newport
quote: Shutdown ritual to use at the end of workday: take a final look at email inbox, transfer new tasks in your mind or scribbled down into an official task list, skim every task in every list, look at the next few days on calendar and at the end make a rough plan for the next day.
refresher: Close the working day by capturing open loops and sketching tomorrow. A trusted plan makes it easier to stop rehearsing unfinished tasks.

links.title: University of Washington · A plan for returning to interrupted work
Cal Newport · On deep breaks

author: Rob Fitzpatrick
quote: Every question we ask carries the very real possibility of biasing the person we're talking to and rendering the whole exercise pointless.
refresher: A leading question can manufacture the answer you wanted. Ask about a specific past experience before introducing your proposed solution.

links.title: GOV.UK · Asking useful questions in user interviews
Rob Fitzpatrick · The Mom Test

author: Rob Fitzpatrick
quote: The measure of usefulness of an early customer conversation is whether it gives us concrete facts about our customers' lives and world views. These facts, in turn, help us improve our business.
refresher: A useful conversation changes what you know about someone’s actual life. Enthusiasm about an idea is weaker evidence than concrete behavior.

links.title: GOV.UK · Asking useful questions in user interviews
Rob Fitzpatrick · The Mom Test

author: Rob Fitzpatrick
quote: Rule of thumb: People know what their problems are, but they don't know how to solve those problems.
refresher: Treat a requested feature as a clue. Ask what the person is trying to accomplish and what makes their current approach frustrating.

links.title: GOV.UK · Learning about people and their needs
Rob Fitzpatrick · The Mom Test

author: Rob Fitzpatrick
quote: Rule of thumb: Watching someone do a task will show you where the problems and inefficiencies really are, not where the customer thinks they are.
refresher: Watching a task reveals workarounds people forget to mention. Ask someone to show you their process, then notice where they hesitate.

links.title: GOV.UK · Observing people in their everyday context
Rob Fitzpatrick · The Mom Test

author: Michael E. Gerber
quote: That Fatal Assumption is; if you understand the technical work of a business, you understand a business that does that technical work.
refresher: Being excellent at the craft does not automatically teach you sales, operations, or management. Treat running the business as a separate skill to learn.

links.title: Center for Creative Leadership · Learning to delegate
EMyth · The three business personalities

author: Michael E. Gerber
quote: The problem is that everybody who goes into business is actually three- people-in-one: The Entrepreneur, The Manager, and The Technician.
refresher: Making the product, organizing the work, and imagining the future are different jobs. Notice which role is taking all your time.

links.title: Atlassian · Clarifying roles and responsibilities
EMyth · The three business personalities

author: Michael E. Gerber
quote: The technician suffering from an Entrepreneurial Seizure takes the work he loves to do and turs it into a job, The work that was born out of love becomes a chore, among a welter of other less familiar and less pleasant chores.
refresher: A business can bury its original craft beneath operational chores. Build repeatable processes around those chores so the craft has room to survive.

links.title: Google SRE · Eliminating repetitive operational work
EMyth · The three business personalities

author: Robert B. Cialdini
quote: The rule of reciprocation says that we should try to repay, in kind, what another person has provided us. There is no human society that does not subscribe to the rule.
refresher: Receiving something can create a felt obligation to return it. Appreciate a favor while evaluating any later request on its own merits.

links.title: Robert Levine · Why persuasion works
Robert Cialdini · Principles of persuasion

author: Robert B. Cialdini
quote: We are nearly obsessed by the desire to be or to appear consistent with what we have already done. Once we have made a choice or taken a stand, we will encounter personal and interpersonal pressures to behave consistently with that commitment.
refresher: A past commitment can pressure you to keep going after the evidence changes. Ask whether you would make the same choice starting fresh.

links.title: Robert Levine · Why persuasion works
Robert Cialdini · Principles of persuasion

author: Robert B. Cialdini
quote: IF two things are presented one after another, if the second item is fairly different from the first, we will tend to see it as more different than it actually is. That works and it's virtually undetectable.
refresher: What you encounter first can distort how the next option feels. Compare alternatives against your actual requirements, not just against each other.

links.title: Harvard Program on Negotiation · Framing and the contrast effect
Robert Cialdini · Principles of persuasion

author: Chris Voss with Tahl Raz
quote: Instead of prioritizing your argument, make your sole focus on the other person and what they have to say.
refresher: Preparing your rebuttal competes with understanding. Give the other person enough room to explain what matters before presenting your own case.

links.title: UC Berkeley · Active listening exercise
The Black Swan Group · Tactical empathy

author: Chris Voss with Tahl Raz
quote: After using tactical empathy to understand the emotions of the other part, you label them translating them into words and then very calmly and respectfully repeating it back to the other side.
refresher: Offer a tentative label such as “It sounds like timing is the concern.” Leave space for correction; the point is understanding, not diagnosing.

links.title: UC Berkeley · Active listening exercise
The Black Swan Group · Tactical empathy

author: Chris Voss with Tahl Raz
quote: Trigger “That’s right” with a summary: paraphrasing + labeling. It’s a stronger version of labeling.
refresher: Combine what happened with why it matters to the other person. Check whether they recognize their perspective in your summary before proposing a solution.

links.title: UC Berkeley · Active listening exercise
The Black Swan Group · Tactical empathy

author: Cole Nussbaumer Knaflic
quote: When you have just a number or two that you want to communicate: use the numbers directly.
refresher: A chart earns its space by making a relationship easier to see. For one or two values, a clear sentence and the numbers may communicate faster.

quote: While pausing before actually building the communication might feel like it's a step that slows you down, in fact it helps ensure that you have a solid understanding of what you want to do before you start creating content, which will save you time down the road.

author: Thich Nhat Hanh
quote: Planning for the future is a part of life. But even planning can only take place in the present moment.
refresher: Thinking about tomorrow is useful; disappearing into it is optional. Notice the act of planning, then return to what is happening now.

author: Thich Nhat Hanh
quote: Conscious breathing: as you breathe in, you say yourself, “Breathing in, I know that I am breathing in”. And as you breathe out, say, “Breathing out, I know that I am breathing out”. You can also use only two words: “In” and “Out”.
refresher: You do not need a special setting to notice one breath. Use the simple rhythm of breathing to reconnect with the present moment.

links.title: UC Berkeley · Mindful breathing exercise

author: Thich Nhat Hanh
quote: You do not have to carry a bell. You can use any sound to remind you to pause, breathe in and out, and enjoy the present moment.
refresher: Let an ordinary sound become a gentle reminder to pause. A notification or kettle can cue a conscious breath before your next action.

links.title: UC Berkeley · Mindful breathing exercise
Plum Village · The art of mindful living

author: Thich Nhat Hanh
quote: In the rush of modern life, we tend to lose touch with the peace that is available in each moment.
refresher: Rushing can make available moments of ease invisible. Choose one ordinary activity today and give it your undivided attention.

links.title: UC Berkeley · A walk for noticing and savoring
Plum Village · The art of mindful living

author: Hermann Hesse
quote: "Meaning and reality were not hidden somewhere behind things, they were in them, in all of them."
refresher: Siddhartha invites attention to life as it is encountered. Before looking for a hidden lesson, notice the texture of the experience itself.

links.title: UC Berkeley · A walk for noticing and savoring
Project Gutenberg · Read Siddhartha

author: Hermann Hesse
quote: "Then he suddenly saw clearly that he was leading a strange life, that he was doing many things that were only a game, that he was quite cheerful and sometimes experienced pleasure, but that real life was flowing past him and did not touch him."
refresher: A full schedule can coexist with a sense of absence. Ask which activity today makes you feel involved in your own life.

links.title: UC Berkeley · A walk for noticing and savoring
Project Gutenberg · Read Siddhartha

author: Hermann Hesse
quote: "A true seeker could not accept any teachings, not if he sincerely wished to find something."

author: Don Norman
quote: A signifier is a mean of signaling the presence of an affordance. It refers to any mark or sound, any perceivable indicator that communicates appropriate behavior to a person.

author: Don Norman

refresher: Repeated mistakes are evidence about the system. Improve feedback, constraints, or recovery before concluding that people simply need to try harder.

author: Don Norman

refresher: A solution begins with the person’s needs and situation. Observe the task in its real context before deciding what to build.

quote: Because much of the knowledge is available in the environment, it is surprising how little we need to learn.

author: Eric Ries
quote: Success is not delivering a feature, success is learning how to solve a customer's problem.

author: Eric Ries
quote: Begin with a clear hypothesis that makes predictions about what is suppose to happen. Then test those predictions empirically.
refresher: Turn a belief into a prediction you can compare with reality. Decide what evidence would change your mind before running the experiment.

quote: In an MVP, when in doubt, simplify. The lesson of the MVP is that any additional work beyond what is required to start learning is waste, no matter ow important it might have seemed at the time.

quote: A startup is a catalyst that transforms ideas into products. As customers interact with those products, they generate feedback and data. We need to focus our energies on minimizing the total time through this feedback loop.

author: Daniel Kahneman
quote: Anchoring effect occurs when people consider a particular value for an unknown quantity before estimating it.
refresher: An initial number can pull later estimates toward it. Form an independent estimate from relevant evidence before treating someone else’s figure as a starting point.

author: Daniel Kahneman
quote: Regression to the mean is the principle according to which extreme results are followed by results nearer to the mean.
refresher: An unusually extreme result often includes temporary influences. Do not assume the next result will be equally extreme or credit every rebound to an intervention.

links.title: Philip Stark, UC Berkeley · Regression and regression to the mean
Daniel Kahneman · Maps of bounded rationality

author: Daniel Kahneman
quote: The "inside view" is the case in exam. The "outside view" are all the other similar cases, that shouldn't be ignored.
refresher: Your project feels unique, but comparable projects contain useful evidence. Start with their actual outcomes, then adjust for differences you can justify.

author: Daniel Kahneman
quote: Ask to people that know everything about the decision: "Imagine we are in the future and the plan we are implementing is a disaster. Take 5 to 10 minutes to write a brief history of what happened"
refresher: Imagine the plan has failed and work backward to possible causes. This makes it easier to surface concerns before commitment becomes expensive.

links.title: Atlassian · Run a project premortem
Daniel Kahneman · Maps of bounded rationality

author: Shunryu Suzuki
quote: "In the beginner's mind there are many possibilities, but in the expert's there are few". The goal of practice is always to keep your beginner's mind.
refresher: Expertise is useful until it prevents you from noticing. Approach a familiar task with one sincere question you have stopped asking.

author: Shunryu Suzuki
quote: If you want to obtain perfect calmness in your zazen, you should not be bothered by the various images you find in your mind. Let them come, and let them go. Then they will be under control.

author: Shunryu Suzuki
quote: When you listen to someone, you should give up all your preconceived ideas and your subjective opinions; you should just listen to him, just observe what his way is.
refresher: Set your interpretation aside long enough to hear the other person. Understanding begins with observing what they actually say.

links.title: UC Berkeley · Active listening exercise

author: Shunryu Suzuki
quote: Do not give up your practice; continue it, knowing your weakness. Your practice cannot be perfect, but without being discouraged by this, you should continue it. This is the secret of practice. Here there is no gaining idea.

author: Richard P. Feynman
quote: I don't know what's the matter with people: they don't learn by understanding; they learn by some other way - by rote, or something. Their knowledge is so fragile!

quote: I sat with the physicists, but after a bit I thought: It would be nice to see what the rest of the world is doing, so I'll sit for a week or two in each of the other groups.

author: Jordan Ellenberg
quote: The armor, said Wald, doesn't go where the bullet holes are. It goes where the bullet holes aren't: the engines.

quote: Every tiny little piece of like can be well approximated by a perfect straight line. The slogan to keep in mind: straight locally, curved globally.

author: Jordan Ellenberg
quote: Mathematics is the extension of common sense by other means. Without the rigorous structure that math provides, common sense can lead you astray.

author: Viktor E. Frankl
quote: We can discover this meaning in life in three different ways: (1) by creating a work or doing a deed; (2) by experiencing something or encountering someone; and (3) by the attitude we take toward unavoidable suffering.
refresher: Frankl points toward contribution, encounter, and the stance we take toward what cannot be changed. Which route has room in your day?

author: Viktor E. Frankl
quote: Live as if you were living already for the second time and as if you had acted the first time as wrongly as you are about to act now.

author: Viktor E. Frankl
quote: In no way suffering is necessary to find meaning. If it were avoidable, the meaningful thing to do would be to remove its cause.

author: Atul Gawande
quote: Whatever the limits and travails we face, we want to retain the autonomy - the freedom - to be authors of our lives.

author: Atul Gawande
quote: How we seek to spend our time may depend on how much time we perceive ourselves to have.

author: Atul Gawande
quote: We think our job is to ensure health and survival. But really it is larger than that. It is to enable well-being.

quote: (Receipts) Printing on thermal paper does not mean adding ink to it. Rather, the ink is already encapsulated within the paper. The act on printing requires only a spark to heat up the paper.

author: Allen B. Downey
quote: Thompson sampling: way of solving the Bayesian Bandit problem by choosing a machine at random so that the probability of choosing each machine is proportional that it is the best. We can draw a single random value from each posterior distribution and select the machine that yields the highest value.

author: Josh Kaufman
quote: Hassle premium: people are almost always willing to pay for things that they believe are too much of a pain to take care of themselves. Where there's a hassle, there's a business opportunity.

Josh Kaufman · Diminishing returns

quote: Charlie generally focuses first on what to avoid-that is, on what not to do-before he considers the affirmative steps he will take in a given situation. "All I want to know is where I'm going to die, so I'll never go there".
refresher: Alongside asking how to succeed, ask what would reliably cause failure. Avoiding preventable mistakes can reveal a simpler path forward.

links.title: Farnam Street · Inversion

author: Charles T. Munger; edited by Peter D. Kaufman
quote: "'We have three baskets for investing: yes, no, and too tough to understand.”
refresher: Not every decision deserves an immediate yes or no. Recognizing that you do not understand a situation can be a useful decision in itself.

links.title: Farnam Street · Circle of competence

author: Charles T. Munger; edited by Peter D. Kaufman
quote: What you need is a latticework of mental models in your head. And you hang your actual experience and your vicarious experience that you get from reading and so forth on this latticework of powerful models. And with that system, things gradually get to fit together in a way that enhances cognition.
refresher: A single explanation makes every problem look alike. Connect ideas from different fields, then check which model actually fits the situation in front of you.

links.title: Farnam Street · A guide to mental models

author: Charles T. Munger; edited by Peter D. Kaufman
quote: Almost everyone thinks he fully recognizes how important incentives and disincentives are in changing cognition and behavior. But this is not often so.
refresher: Before explaining behavior as a personality trait, inspect what gets rewarded. A sensible person can produce an undesirable result when the reward system points that way.

links.title: Farnam Street · A guide to mental models

author: Charles T. Munger; edited by Peter D. Kaufman
quote: Analytic rigor: Use of the scientific method and effective checklists minimizes errors and omissions.
refresher: Expertise does not make memory reliable under pressure. Externalize critical checks so routine omissions do not undermine otherwise sound judgment.

links.title: Farnam Street · A guide to mental models

author: Gergely Orosz
quote: Record key work each week, including important code changes, code reviews, design documents, discussions and planning, helping out others, postmortems, and anything else which takes time and has an impact. Former Stripe software engineer Julia Evans calls this a “brag document”.
refresher: Record contributions while they are fresh, including reviews, mentoring, and maintenance. A concrete record helps you recognize progress that a list of shipped features misses.

source.file: Orosz G. - The Software Engineer_s Guidebook.docx

links.title: Julia Evans · Write a brag document

author: Gergely Orosz
quote: My suggestion is to avoid asking for personal feedback. Instead, ask for feedback about something specific you did, or worked on.
refresher: “How did I do?” is difficult to answer usefully. Ask about a concrete artifact or moment, such as whether a design explanation made the trade-offs clear.

source.file: Orosz G. - The Software Engineer_s Guidebook.docx

links.title: Manager Tools · A practical feedback model (PDF)

author: Gergely Orosz
concept: Feedback is input, not an order
quote: Take feedback seriously, but remember that it’s opinion and not a directive. Just because people give you feedback, doesn’t mean you need to act on it. Listen to what they have to say, then figure out if it’s valid.
refresher: Listen carefully, then evaluate the observation against your goals and other evidence. You can take feedback seriously without following every suggestion.

source.file: Orosz G. - The Software Engineer_s Guidebook.docx

links.title: Manager Tools · A practical feedback model (PDF)

author: Gergely Orosz
quote: Stand out in results, impact, and numbers. Define the impact of your work, ideally with numbers.
refresher: Explain who benefited and what changed because of your work. Use numbers when they clarify the result; avoid replacing meaningful outcomes with impressive-looking activity counts.

source.file: Orosz G. - The Software Engineer_s Guidebook.docx

links.title: Staff Engineer · Work on what matters

author: Gergely Orosz
quote: Keep a “cheat sheet” document in which you record everything that’s new. This could be acronyms and their meanings, build commands, bookmarks to key resources, and much more.
refresher: Capture unfamiliar terms, commands, and useful references while learning a system. A small searchable guide saves you from repeatedly solving the same orientation problems.

source.file: Orosz G. - The Software Engineer_s Guidebook.docx

links.title: Julia Evans · Keeping “today I learned” notes

author: Harry Percival and Bob Gregory
quote: So the first part of the DIP says that our business code shouldn’t depend on technical details; instead, both should use abstractions. Why? Broadly, because we want to be able to change them independently of each other.
refresher: Keep business rules independent of replaceable infrastructure. An abstraction lets the database or transport change without forcing the core behavior to change with it.

source.file: Percival H. - Architecture Patterns with Python.docx

links.title: Alistair Cockburn · Ports and adapters architecture
Cosmic Python · Abstractions and dependency inversion

author: Harry Percival and Bob Gregory
quote: Behavior should come first and drive our storage requirements. After all, our customers don’t care about the data model. They care about what the system does; otherwise they’d just use a spreadsheet.
refresher: Start with what the system must do for people. Let those use cases shape the data model, rather than treating database tables as the product specification.

source.file: Percival H. - Architecture Patterns with Python.docx

links.title: Martin Fowler · Domain logic and the database
Cosmic Python · Domain modeling

author: Harry Percival and Bob Gregory
quote: When we hear our business stakeholders using unfamiliar words, or using terms in a specific way, we should listen to understand the deeper meaning and encode their hard-won experience into our software.
refresher: Specialized vocabulary often encodes important business distinctions. Learn what stakeholders mean and preserve those distinctions in the names and behavior of your software.

source.file: Percival H. - Architecture Patterns with Python.docx

links.title: Martin Fowler · Building a shared domain language
Cosmic Python · Domain modeling

author: Harry Percival and Bob Gregory
quote: Whenever we have a business concept that has data but no identity, we often choose to represent it using the Value Object pattern. A value object is any domain object that is uniquely identified by the data it holds; we usually make them immutable.
refresher: Some things are defined by their attributes rather than a unique identity. Two equivalent measurements or amounts can be interchangeable; immutability helps preserve that meaning.

source.file: Percival H. - Architecture Patterns with Python.docx

links.title: Martin Fowler · Value objects
Cosmic Python · Domain modeling

author: Harry Percival and Bob Gregory
quote: Entities, unlike values, have identity equality. We can change their values, and they are still recognizably the same thing. Batches, in our example, are entities. We can allocate lines to a batch, or change the date that we expect it to arrive, and it will still be the same entity.
refresher: An entity stays the same entity even when its attributes change. Model identity explicitly when tracking something through time, such as an order whose status changes.

source.file: Percival H. - Architecture Patterns with Python.docx

links.title: Martin Fowler · Entities, value objects, and services
Cosmic Python · Domain modeling

author: Cathy O’Neil
quote: Our own values and desire influence our choices, from the data we choose to collect to the questions we ask. Models are opinions embedded in mathematics.
refresher: A mathematical model embeds decisions about what to measure and optimize. Inspect those choices before treating its output as a neutral description of reality.

links.title: Google · Fairness in machine learning

author: Cathy O’Neil
concept: A proxy is not the target
quote: The folks building WMDs routinely lack data for the behaviors they're most interested in. So they substitute stand-in data, or proxies. These correlations are discriminatory, and some of them are illegal.
refresher: A convenient measurement can stand in for something you cannot observe directly. Ask where that substitution breaks down and whose circumstances it misrepresents.

links.title: Google · Fairness in machine learning

author: Cathy O’Neil
quote: Whether or not a model works is also matter of opinion. A key component of a model is its definition of success.
refresher: A system can perform well against its chosen metric while failing the people affected. Ask whose outcome the metric rewards and what it leaves invisible.

links.title: Google · Fairness in machine learning

author: Cathy O’Neil
quote: These are the three elements of a WMD: Opacity, Scale, and Damage.
refresher: O’Neil’s warning concerns systems that combine hard-to-question decisions with wide reach and damaging consequences. Consider recourse and affected people alongside predictive performance.

links.title: Google · Fairness in machine learning

author: Cathy O’Neil
quote: The human victims of WMDs are held to a far higher standard of evidence than the algorithms themselves.
refresher: If people bear the consequences of a score, they need a meaningful way to challenge errors. Accountability includes examining the model, not only demanding better evidence from those it judges.

links.title: Google · Fairness in machine learning

author: Yuval Noah Harari
concept: Culture can change faster than genes
quote: Ever since the Cognitive Revolution, Sapiens have been able to change their behaviour quickly, transmitting new behaviours to future generations without any need of genetic environmental change.
refresher: Learned practices can spread through teaching and imitation without waiting for biological evolution. Keep cultural explanations distinct from claims that a behavior is genetically inevitable.

links.title: Smithsonian · Language and symbols

author: Yuval Noah Harari
quote: Three main factors prevent people from realizing that the order organising their lives exists only in their imagination: the imagined order is embedded in the material world, the imagined order shapes our desires, the imagined order is inter-subjective.
refresher: In Harari’s framing, institutions become powerful when people coordinate around shared meanings. “Imagined” does not mean inconsequential: collectively accepted rules can shape very real opportunities.

links.title: Smithsonian · Language and symbols

author: Yuval Noah Harari
quote: Money is anything that people are willing to use in order to represent systematically the value of other things for the purpose of exchanging goods and services. Is a new inter-subject reality that exists solely in people's shared imagination.
refresher: Money works partly because people expect others to accept it. That shared expectation connects strangers who do not need to agree on much else.

links.title: Bank of England · What is money?

author: Yuval Noah Harari
quote: There is an iron rule of history that what looks inevitable in hindsight was far from obvious at the time.
refresher: Knowing the ending makes earlier events look more inevitable than they were. Reconstruct the information available at the time before judging a past decision.

links.title: Baruch Fischhoff · Studying the past without hindsight (PDF)

author: Yuval Noah Harari
quote: When evaluating global happiness, it is wrong to count the happiness only of the upper classes, of Europeans or of men. Perhaps it is also wrong to consider only the happiness of humans.
refresher: A claim about progress depends on whose experience is included. Widen the frame beyond visible winners and consider those who bear costs without having a voice.

links.title: Peter Singer · The why and how of effective altruism

book: A Short History of Nearly Everything
author: Bill Bryson
quote: Elements were normally grouped in two ways - either by atomic weight or by common properties. Mendeleyev’s breakthrough was to see that the two could be combined in a single table.
refresher: Organizing elements by recurring properties made gaps in the table informative. A useful classification does more than label what is known; it suggests what to look for next.

source.file: A short history of nearly everything notes.html

links.title: Royal Society of Chemistry · Explore the periodic table

book: A Short History of Nearly Everything
author: Bill Bryson
quote: He measured the velocity of light with great precision, but the speed of light turned out to be the same in all directions and at all seasons.
refresher: The speed of light in a vacuum is invariant for inertial observers. Unlike an ordinary moving object, light does not simply acquire extra speed because its source is moving.

source.file: A short history of nearly everything notes.html

links.title: NIST · The speed of light and SI units

book: A Short History of Nearly Everything
author: Bill Bryson
quote: If you had to reduce scientific history to one important statement it would be “all things are made of atoms”.
refresher: Everyday materials are built from atoms arranged and bonded in different ways. Their microscopic organization helps explain the very different properties you notice at human scale.

source.file: A short history of nearly everything notes.html

links.title: Royal Society of Chemistry · Elements and their properties

book: A Short History of Nearly Everything
author: Bill Bryson
quote: All living things have within them an isotope of carbon called carbon-14, which begins to decay at a measurable rate the instant they die.
refresher: A correction to the note: carbon-14 decays during life too. After death, replenishment stops, so the changing isotope ratio can help estimate when once-living material stopped exchanging carbon.

source.file: A short history of nearly everything notes.html

links.title: National Park Service · Radiometric age dating

book: A Short History of Nearly Everything
author: Bill Bryson
quote: The right kind of planet: the molten interior helped building the atmosphere, provided us with the magnetic field that shield us from cosmic radiation and gave us tectonics.
refresher: Earth’s interior helps generate a magnetic field that interacts with charged particles from space. Together with the atmosphere, it shapes the protective environment in which we live.

source.file: A short history of nearly everything notes.html

links.title: NASA · Earth’s magnetosphere

book: How to Win Friends and Influence People
author: Dale Carnegie
quote: You can make more friends in two months by becoming genuinely interested in other people than you can in two years by trying to get other people interested in you.
refresher: Connection often begins by being curious about another person’s world. Ask a question you actually want answered, then make room for the answer.

source.file: How to win friends and influence people notes.html

links.title: The Gottman Institute · Four mindful listening principles

book: How to Win Friends and Influence People
author: Dale Carnegie
quote: Remember that a person's name is to that person the sweetest and most important sound in any language:
refresher: Using someone’s name attentively can signal recognition. Learn how they pronounce it and what they prefer to be called, rather than repeating it mechanically.

source.file: How to win friends and influence people notes.html

links.title: The Gottman Institute · Small things often

book: How to Win Friends and Influence People
author: Dale Carnegie
quote: You want a feeling that you are important in your little world. You don't want to listen to cheap, insincere flattery, but you do crave sincere appreciation. How? When? Where? The answer is: All the time, everywhere
refresher: Praise is more meaningful when it names something real. Point to a specific contribution and explain why it mattered instead of reaching for generic flattery.

source.file: How to win friends and influence people notes.html

links.title: Manager Tools · A practical feedback model (PDF)

book: How to Win Friends and Influence People
author: Dale Carnegie
quote: 'If you argue and rankle and contradict, you may achieve a victory sometimes; but it will be an empty victory because you will never get your opponent's good will.'
refresher: A debate can end with your argument intact and the other person less willing to cooperate. Decide whether the goal is a point scored or a problem solved together.

source.file: How to win friends and influence people notes.html

links.title: The Gottman Institute · Listen without getting defensive

book: How to Win Friends and Influence People
author: Dale Carnegie
quote: Be honest. Look for areas where you can can admit error and say so. Apologize for your mistakes.
refresher: A clear acknowledgment of your mistake can interrupt a defensive exchange. Name what you got wrong and what you will do next, without making the apology a counterattack.

source.file: How to win friends and influence people notes.html

author: Erich Fromm
quote: Is love an art? Then it requires knowledge and effort. Or is love a pleasant sensation, which to experience is a matter of chance, something one `falls into' if one is lucky? This little book is based on the former premise, while undoubtedly the majority of people today believe in the latter.
refresher: Fromm treats loving as a capacity to develop, not only a feeling to discover. Look at the habits through which you give someone care and attention.

source.file: Fromm E. - The Art of Loving_.docx

links.title: The Gottman Institute · Small things often

author: Erich Fromm
quote: Beyond the element of giving the active character of love becomes evident in the fact that it always implies certain basic elements. common to all forms of love. These are care, responsibility, respect and knowledge.
refresher: Fromm connects love with care, responsibility, respect, and knowledge. Use the four together: wanting someone’s good is different from assuming you already know what they need.

source.file: Fromm E. - The Art of Loving_.docx

links.title: The Gottman Institute · Four mindful listening principles

author: Erich Fromm
quote: Responsibility could easily deteriorate into domination and possessiveness, were it not for a third component of love, respect. Respect is not fear and awe; it denotes, in accordance with the root of the word (respicere, to look at), the ability to see a person as he is to be aware of his unique individuality.
refresher: Caring for a person does not grant ownership of their choices. Make room for the person they actually are, rather than the version you want them to become.

source.file: Fromm E. - The Art of Loving_.docx

links.title: The Gottman Institute · Four mindful listening principles

author: Erich Fromm
quote: The affirmation of one's own life, happiness, growth, freedom is rooted in one's capacity to love, i.e. in care,. respect, responsibility, and knowledge. If an individual is able to love productively, he loves himself too; if he can love only others, he cannot love at all.
refresher: Fromm’s account of love includes regard for your own life and growth. Caring for others need not require treating your own needs as worthless.

source.file: Fromm E. - The Art of Loving_.docx

links.title: The Gottman Institute · Small things often

author: Erich Fromm
quote: A third factor is patience. Patience is necessary if you want to achieve anything. If one is after quick results, one never learns an art.
refresher: Deep capacities develop through repeated practice, not an instant result. Give relationships time to grow while remaining attentive to what your actions are contributing.

source.file: Fromm E. - The Art of Loving_.docx

links.title: The Gottman Institute · Small things often

author: Peter Thiel with Blake Masters
quote: Successful people find value in unexpected places, and they do this by thinking about business from first principles instead of formulas.
refresher: Separate a problem’s actual constraints from familiar ways of solving it. Copying a successful formula may miss the conditions that made it work.

links.title: Farnam Street · A guide to mental models

author: Peter Thiel with Blake Masters
quote: Going from 0 to 1, or progressing vertically, is harder to imagine because it requires doing something nobody else has ever done.
refresher: Thiel distinguishes improving or spreading an existing approach from making something newly possible. Ask what your idea enables that people could not do before.

links.title: Paul Graham · How to get startup ideas

author: Peter Thiel with Blake Masters
quote: Every startup should start with a very small market. The perfect target is a small group of particular people concentrated together and served by few or no competitors.
refresher: A small, clearly defined group can have an urgent problem you can solve well. Learn to serve that group deeply before broadening your reach.

links.title: Paul Graham · How to get startup ideas

author: Peter Thiel with Blake Masters
quote: You can't find secrets without looking for them. If you think something hard is impossible, you'll never even start trying to achieve it.
refresher: Unexplored questions remain invisible if you assume all the useful answers are known. Investigate a neglected problem before concluding that it cannot be solved.

links.title: Paul Graham · How to get startup ideas

author: Peter Thiel with Blake Masters
quote: For a company to be valuable it must grow and endure, if you focus on near-term growth above all else, you miss the most important question you should be asking: will this business still be around a decade from now?
refresher: Early growth is only part of the story. Ask what will keep the product useful and the organization viable after the initial excitement fades.

links.title: NFX · Network effects as a source of defensibility
Y Combinator · Peter Thiel on durable businesses (video)

author: Reed Hastings and Erin Meyer
concept: The hidden cost of a rule
quote: Errors that cost company money. Each time this happened, I put a process in place to prevent that mistake from occurring again. Policies and control processes became foundational. We failed to innovate quickly, and were unable to adapt.
refresher: A rule introduced after one mistake can burden every future decision. Periodically compare the problem a process prevents with the time and adaptability it costs.

links.title: Google SRE · Eliminating repetitive operational work
Netflix · Culture memo

author: Reed Hastings and Erin Meyer
quote: Coach your employees to give and receive feedback effectively, following the 4A guidelines (giver side: Aim to assist, Actionable, receiver side: Appreciate, Accept or discard).
refresher: The four-part framework asks givers to assist and be actionable, and receivers to appreciate feedback while deciding whether to use it. Candor is a skill, not permission for cruelty.

links.title: Manager Tools · A practical feedback model (PDF)

author: Reed Hastings and Erin Meyer
quote: In order to lead with context, you need to have high talent density, your goal needs to be innovation (not error prevention), and you need to be operating in a loosely coupled system.
refresher: Hastings and Meyer make freedom conditional on capable teams, loose coupling, and a goal of innovation. Match the amount of control to the work’s actual consequences.

links.title: Atlassian · Clarify who owns a decision with DACI
Netflix · Culture memo

author: Reed Hastings and Erin Meyer
quote: In a fast and innovative company, ownership of critical, big-ticket decisions should be dispersed across the workforce at all different levels, not allocated according to hierarchical status.
refresher: Put decisions near people with relevant information rather than automatically sending everything upward. Clarify who owns the choice and which context they need.

links.title: Atlassian · Clarify who owns a decision with DACI
Netflix · Culture memo

author: Reed Hastings and Erin Meyer
quote: Teach your employees that when a bet fails, they should sunshine it openly.
refresher: Make an unsuccessful experiment visible enough for others to learn from it. Explain the assumption, what happened, and what you will change on the next attempt.

links.title: Google SRE · Learning from failure with blameless postmortems
Netflix · Culture memo

author: Jay Sullivan
quote: Instead of thinking, "What am I trying to convey?" we should ask ourselves, "Why is he reading my email or attending this meeting? What does she hope to get out of this presentation?"
refresher: Before explaining your content, identify why the audience is there. Organize the message around what they need to understand or decide.

links.title: Duarte · Your audience is the hero

author: Jay Sullivan
quote: Is short: key message limited to one sentence, preferably fewer than 10 words long. Consider breaking the content into smaller sentences to help your listeners. Ask: "Will my audience be able to repeat this message to someone else after this meeting?"
refresher: Reduce the central message to something a listener can repeat accurately. Supporting detail should reinforce that idea instead of competing with it.

links.title: Duarte · The Big Idea

author: Jay Sullivan
quote: Use simple language: big words do not impress anyone. Big ideas do. In a professional setting, you're not graded on smarts. People assume you are smart. You're graded on having impact.
refresher: Specialized language is useful when it adds precision for the reader. Otherwise, familiar words make the idea easier to understand and act on.

links.title: Google · Choose clear, consistent words

author: Jay Sullivan
quote: He remember the teaching point from the program because of the story, and he remembered the story because stories stick with us.
refresher: A story connects a point to people, choices, and consequences. Use a concrete example that helps the audience reconstruct the idea later.

links.title: Duarte · Structure a story that moves people

author: Jay Sullivan
quote: Set actions steps at the end of the meeting (who does what by when).
refresher: A useful meeting ends with more than general agreement. Record the next action, the person responsible, and the time by which it should happen.

links.title: Atlassian · Meeting notes with owners and action items
Jay Sullivan · Simply Said resources

book: The Subtle Art of Not Giving a F*ck
author: Mark Manson
quote: The key to a good life is not giving a fuck about more; it's giving a fuck about less, giving a fuck about only what is true and immediate and important.
refresher: Attention is finite, so treating everything as equally important makes priorities disappear. Decide which commitments deserve your effort and which noise can pass.

book: The Subtle Art of Not Giving a F*ck
author: Mark Manson

book: The Subtle Art of Not Giving a F*ck
author: Mark Manson
quote: Good values are: reality-based, socially constructive, immediate and controllable. Bad values are the opposite.

author: Mark Manson
quote: Certainty is the enemy of growth. Being wrong opens up to the possibility of change. Being wrong brings the opportunity of growth.
